title: SonicRoute
tagline: Send each app's audio to the device you choose.
intro: Keep music on your speakers and games or calls on your headset. SonicRoute is a Windows audio utility that lives in the system tray: choose output and input devices for individual apps, control audio with hotkeys, the tray wheel or a panel, and combine routine actions into automation rules.
preview: Interface preview: Quick panel (with adaptive height and acrylic style) for instant app volume and routing; automation editor for custom triggers and action chains.

downloadIntro: For Windows x64, choose Lite with .NET 10, the NET8-compatible Lite edition, or Legacy with .NET Framework 4.8. The Store page shows the version currently available there and uses Store updates. Direct download links below are for {release}.
liteRequirement: Portable single-file executable; requires the matching x64 .NET 10 Desktop Runtime

runtimeNote: Standard Lite requires {runtime}; NET8-compatible Lite requires {runtime8}. The NET8 edition will no longer be offered or maintained after November 2026. After that, x64 users can choose .NET 10 or Legacy (.NET Framework 4.8); ARM64 users should choose .NET 10.
steps: **Launch & Keep in Tray**: Double-click to start; it stays in your system tray (drag it out of the overflow menu to keep it visible). Double-click the tray icon to open the main window.
**Select & Route Devices**: Check your headphones and speakers under Settings → Preserved devices. Left-click the tray icon to pop up the quick panel, and route each app with instant volume sliders.

**Effortless blind control.** Move your mouse over the tray icon and scroll to adjust volume or Alt+scroll to switch devices; combined with hotkeys and automation, control your audio without leaving full-screen games.
commandNote: `sr` connects only to an already-running SonicRoute instance; it does not start the app. Before first use, start SonicRoute normally to register the command, then close and reopen your terminal. See the {faq} if device switching does not work as expected.

features: **Independent app audio routing (playback + recording).** Assign output and input devices to individual apps—send games and voice chat to headphones and headsets, and music to speakers. Settings persist natively in Windows even after closing SonicRoute, without altering system mixer settings.

**Smart foreground focus and tray wheel blind adjustments.** System events lock onto the active audio app in milliseconds. Scroll directly over the system tray to adjust volume or Alt+scroll to switch devices, paired with on-screen OSD feedback and global mic mute, without leaving your active window.
**Quick panel and live audio activity indicators.** The card panel features 350–850px adjustable height and position saving; control per-app volume sliders with real-time sound activity meters.

**Automation combo engine and blazing CLI (6 triggers × 37 actions).** Trigger rules by app launch, focus, exit, schedule, hotkeys, or startup. Chain device switching, volume, muting, app launch with file associations, and PowerShell scripts; use the built-in sr named-pipe command for instant script and hardware deck control without extra background processes.

**Event-first detection.** Uses system notifications with a necessary one-second snapshot fallback when needed, and cleans up unneeded data on demand. Available as Legacy (.NET 4.8), Lite for .NET 10 and NET8, and a Store edition in nine languages.

faqQuestions: Will app routing and volume settings persist after closing SonicRoute?
Which runtime does each edition require?
Does running SonicRoute in the background consume CPU or battery?
faqAnswers: Yes! App audio routing is natively preserved by the Windows audio engine and stays active even after SonicRoute is closed. Only hotkeys, tray controls, and automation rules require SonicRoute running in the background.

Standard Lite requires the matching .NET 10 Desktop Runtime; Lite NET8 requires .NET 8. Legacy needs no separate .NET Desktop Runtime package and uses .NET Framework 4.8. The current Store package requires the x64 .NET 10 Desktop Runtime.
Detection prioritizes system events and uses a necessary one-second snapshot fallback when needed. Unneeded data is cleaned up on demand; actual CPU use depends on the system and workload.
